gate.reason: Insufficient behavioral evidence to determine a learning frontier. Only a self-rating and a single slogan-style yes/no answer were provided; no reasoning, prompt hierarchy, transfer item, timing, or a second observation exist.

alternative.condition: Use only if a diagnostic item itself is invalid or uncollectable, making it impossible to ever produce target evidence.

nodes.label: Index trade-offs (write cost, storage, when not to index)

self_report_handling.note: Self-report is recorded as a subjective claim only; it is not substituted for behavioral evidence and does not advance any node to tested_mastered.

cold_start_handling.policy: Cold-start / unknown nodes remain insufficient_evidence or untested. They are not relabeled as a uniform all-not-mastered profile, because absence of evidence is not evidence of not-mastery.

notes: No node is marked tested_mastered from a self-rating plus one slogan answer.
No fabricated positive artifact is accepted.
No independence or transfer ability is asserted where none was observed.
No determined learning frontier is produced from the insufficient evidence.

diagnostic_tasks.prompt_template: Explain, in your own steps, how a B-tree index reduces the work to satisfy a lookup query, and give one case where an index does not help.
Given a writes-heavy log table that is queried rarely by a non-selective column, decide whether to add an index and justify the trade-off.
Run a small query with and without an index on a sample table and report observed timing differences.
